scope: One source-qualified unpolarized hydrogen Ly-alpha component in a declared isolated two-level Sobolev model. No full cosmological source, nuclear network, or thermodynamic closure is certified.

sources.title: Persistent Lines of Neutral Hydrogen (H I)
sources.locator: 1215.66824 and 1215.67364 Angstrom rows; Aki heading is 10^8 s^-1
facts: Vacuum fine-component wavelengths, spontaneous emission coefficients, lower/upper J values and level energies.
limitations: This is the currently accessible NIST Handbook table, not a fresh ASD dynamic query or a claim about the newest ASD release.
Numerical uncertainties are not supplied on this table. Tabulated digits are finite-precision data, not exact physical constants.
Tabulated line intensities are not population boundary conditions.

sources.title: Atomic Spectroscopy: Atomic Lifetimes / Regularities and Scaling
sources.locator: Hydrogen spectral-series table and footnotes b,c
facts: The 1-2 row has lambda=1215.67 Angstrom, lower g=2, upper g=8, A=4.699e8 s^-1.
Here g=2 n^2 counts the whole principal shell, not only 2p.
sources.reuse: Convention countercheck only; do not import its g and A into an n_2p variable.

sources.title: Lyman-alpha transfer in primordial hydrogen recombination
facts: Sobolev escape probability and opacity difference g*x_l-x_u.
The incident f_plus is the blue-side photon occupation; it may contain feedback.
limitations: Equations assume the stated Sobolev/line model; the paper itself studies corrections beyond that approximation.
The Bianchi directional substitution and tensor injection map below are direct derivations for this unit, not formulas quoted from this paper.

sources.title: Time-Dependent Corrections to the Ly-alpha Escape Probability During Cosmological Hydrogen Recombination
facts: Occupation convention f_nu=c^2 I_nu/(2 h nu^3).
Standard Sobolev beta and its thick limit.
Real emission/absorption, resonant scattering and profile/time corrections must be distinguished.
limitations: Several source terms there explicitly neglect stimulated emission for f<<1; use Hirata-Forbes equations (1)-(3) for the exact finite-f toy/source contract.

recommended_contract.rationale: A single explicit J component ties the tabulated A and vacuum wavelength to one unambiguous population. The J=1/2 choice avoids a rank-two atomic alignment degree of freedom within an unpolarized scalar-population contract.
recommended_contract.no_claim: This is not an isolated physical description of the complete cosmological Ly-alpha doublet, whose overlapping line transfer and feedback need a separate owner.
recommended_contract.population: n_l and n_u count all magnetic substates of the selected lower and upper J levels per physical volume in the matter rest frame. No per-m-substate population and no whole-n=2 shell population.
required_owned_inputs: f_plus at the line blue boundary, dimensionless and with provenance
recommended_contract.isotropy: Factorization into scalar D times B,Q requires direction-independent blue-boundary f_plus, unpolarized populations and direction-independent rest-frame line emissivity.

conditions: A common-frequency/common-A approximation must be explicitly chosen, or keep and sum the two component source rates.
A statistical sublevel split n_2p3/2=2*n_2p1/2 is an additional population closure, not implied by the NIST intensity column.
A single beta of a summed opacity does not in general equal the sum of two component escape rates; shared/overlapping line transfer needs its own derivation.

whole_n2_shell.warning: Do not mix with collapsed 2p g=3 or a selected fine J population.

collapsed_comparison.fine_split_note: Difference of the tabulated wavelengths; not an uncertainty estimate. A collapsed-frequency model discards this splitting.
collapsed_comparison.derived_shell_relation: Under statistical shell occupancy n_2p=(6/8)*n_2, (3/4)*A_2p approximately yields the shell-average A; this is a convention explanation, not a physical mixing rate.

formulas.domain: Delta>0 for the inherited positive-t escape kernel. Inversion is excluded.

formulas.note: Unpolarized occupation per photon state; f_plus is evaluated on the blue boundary, not a bolometric energy density.

formulas.sign: R>0 means net downward transition / net line-photon creation.

formulas.domain: H>0, Delta>0, q(n)>0, nonrelativistic comoving line, local Sobolev approximation. Shear sign must agree with the parent geodesic redshift convention.
An isotropic D is required to factor it outside the angular average.

formulas.note: Collision/source contributions only. Physical-volume dilution and boundary propagation terms must be added by their existing owners.
Use the locked lambda for this unit's energy; do not independently round a second energy input.

formulas.domain: Recoil-free isolated bound-bound exchange. This is not an ionic-yield or gas-heating source.

formulas.note: Effective escaped-radiation anisotropic-stress injection rate for the declared Sobolev source. It is not an instantaneous stored radiation tensor, not matter stress, and not a derivation of the full microscopic line collision tensor.

formulas.domain: T>0; use the same epsilon and population convention. This local cancellation does not prove global LTE or thermodynamic closure.
Delta>0. The un-divided D remains the preferred definition near zero opacity.

finite_accuracy_policy.comment: The inherited angular numeric tolerance can test integration/algebra at locked input values. It cannot establish 1e-8 physical atomic-data accuracy or accuracy of the isolated Sobolev model.
parent_to_freeze_before_execution: Finite source cases and resource cap
Population/boundary provenance for any claimed physical trajectory

exclusions: No reuse of shell-averaged g=8/A=4.699e8 in a 2p population.
No externally fitted full cosmological model.
No source-owned blue-boundary radiation synthesized from unrelated completed pilot populations.
No claim that two isolated fine-component rates constitute overlapping-doublet radiative transfer.
No recoil, polarization, redistribution correction, multi-photon correction or full ionic-yield closure.
discovery_cautions: SciSpace results contain duplicate papers and a year inconsistent with the primary arXiv record. They were used for discovery only; primary PDFs own formula and date attribution.
